scope.description: The local AppendFuture consumption boundary in Raft.pipelineDecode, beginning with delivery of a future through AppendPipeline.Consumer and ending at response access or the resulting replication progress report. Check successful and failed completion separately.
assumptions: The delivered future belongs to the pipeline and exposes its associated request.
The test invokes the actual pipelineDecode implementation with initialized replication state.
A controlled interface implementation may deliver a completed failed future; Consumer's contract does not restrict delivery to successful futures.
excluded: Proof that a built-in follower produces an error together with Success=true in a legal cluster history
Proof of incorrect commitment, application, or client completion
Full request-response correlation across network failures
Other transport variants and deployment activation
Shutdown and peer-replacement correctness beyond the exercised consumption boundary

properties.reason: Actual result fields are compared after independent prerequisite association

adaptations: Replace the pipeline and future with controlled implementations of the supplied interfaces; retain the actual pipelineDecode, updateLastAppended, and commitment code.
Supply immutable completed error status and explicitly controlled response fields. Success=true on a failed future is an artificial input, not an observed built-in transport response.
Instrument Response access and stop the decoder after the exercised iteration through its existing stop channel.
Initialize isolated replication state directly instead of starting a cluster. Observe the real commitment match map after decoder completion.
Disable legacy telemetry duplication; no protocol decision is changed.
boundaries: Proof that a built-in follower produces an error together with Success=true in a legal cluster history
Proof of incorrect commitment, application, or client completion
Full request-response correlation across network failures
Other transport variants and deployment activation
Shutdown and peer-replacement correctness beyond the exercised consumption boundary
Artificial failed-future response contents are controlled interface inputs; they are not evidence of a built-in producer emitting those fields.
The match-map comparison detects an effective progress update in this initialized state, not every possible invocation of commitment.match.
The Error marker is set immediately before its synchronous return; the controlled Error implementation has no blocking or intervening calls, and the decoder invokes the methods sequentially.
No observation here establishes incorrect commitment, application, client completion, or deployment activation.
Missing result events, timeout, panic, and compilation errors are execution outcomes, not completed property comparisons.
This is a provisional correspondence judgment for the supplied check and observations, not overall implementation correctness or an independent reproduction.

The commitment implementation and additional initialization dependencies cited by the plan are not attached. The observed map change and the attached updateLastAppended call support the immediate scoped comparison; commitment aggregation semantics are not independently reviewed.
Built-in production of a failed response with Success=true, legal cluster-history reachability, deployment activation, and incorrect commitment or client completion remain unresolved.

The check does not cover all response contents, repeated or ineffective progress reports, empty requests, peer replacement, shutdown behavior, or other transport variants. Broader bad outcomes could remain even if these two local properties held.
The observations exercise violations in the current implementation; they do not establish that the harness terminates or provides complete coverage for every alternative implementation.
